summary: You can't play it on Switch, but unsanctioned Android ports could be coming soon.
body: TL;DR Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 64 has been fully decompiled, opening the door to unofficial native ports. The 1999 platform fighter hasn’t been available through official means for several years and isn’t currently playable on Nintendo Switch consoles. We aren’t aware of any ports made from the newly decompiled code yet, but we expect they’ll start appearing soon. Aside from some high-profile rereleases, present-day Nintendo is notoriously stingy when it comes to providing easy, legitimate access to its immense back catalog of classic games. This, in part, has inspired fans to take matters into their own hands by decompiling old favorites, recreating their source code so the games can be easily (if unofficially) ported to modern platforms like Windows or Android. Now, another classic that’s been inaccessible on modern hardware is ripe for porting: 1999’s Super Smash Bros. has been fully decompiled. As shared on Decomp.dev , Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 64 is now “100.00% decompiled,” meaning the game’s source code has been completely recreated and it’s ready to be ported. title: Luminate to Add Labels to AI Music Later This Year
summary: The move follows several announcements by streaming services and the record business to pursue labels for AI content earlier this summer.
body: On Tuesday (Aug. 25), entertainment data company Luminate announced a new framework for AI music. This includes the addition of labels for AI-generated content on its platform, starting later this year, which will be visible to its customers and partners. The move comes just weeks after Apple Music and Spotify announced plans for their own versions of labeling for AI music by the end of 2026. Luminate’s system will rely on a combination of its proprietary identification technology and collaborations with major streaming services and AI music companies to determine which songs should be labeled. A label stating “AI Generated” will be added to any song or artist profile identified through their system, and, in the case of false positives, artists and labels can go through a “dedicated review process” to have the labels reconsidered. title: How Sam Fender & Olivia Dean’s ‘Rein Me In’ Became the U.K.’s Longest-Running No. 1 Single Ever
summary: The song now holds the all-time record for the longest-running U.K. No. 1 single.
body: Sam Fender ’s show at the London Stadium in June 2025 remains momentous for many reasons. It was the midway point of the rollout of his Mercury Prize-winning LP People Watching , and also his largest ever headline show. But perhaps the most consequential moment from it came midway through the set, album deep cut “Rein Me In” got an airing, with the show’s support act Olivia Dean , then a rising star, joining on vocals for a new verse. Now their careers — and that song — appear unstoppable. “Rein Me In” is in record-breaking territory on the U.K.’s Official Singles Chart. The track has earned 22 weeks at No. 1, and became the longest-running No. 1 single of the 21st century after 16, surpassing Drake’s “Hotline Bling.” It has now pulled clear of Frankie Laine’s “I Believe” in the all time rankings, which notched 18 weeks at the summit back in 1953, to become the longest-running U.K. No. 1 single ever. In February, it earned the BRIT Awards’ publicly voted song of the year prize, with Dean and Fender on hand to collect the prize in Manchester. body: As is the case with millions of users around the world, I’ve been a loyal Spotify subscriber for as long as I can remember. The app works well across Android and iOS, there’s a great selection of music, and features like Jam and Spotify Connect have made my listening experience much more seamless across audio devices at home. I was happy to pay for the Premium Duo plan — until it was sneakily taken away. Spotify removed the Duo plan in India around November 2025, but as I had subscribed to it long before, I was able to continue with it, as it should be. Then came the email, one July morning this year, saying my Premium Duo plan was canceled due to an “issue” with my payment method. Nothing had changed, so it didn’t make any sense. It’s no secret that Nintendo has historically taken an extremely strict stance against emulators and people using its IP without permission. A few months ago, the company sent DMCA notices to take down several Switch emulators whose code was hosted on GitHub. Now, the company has thrown another proverbial Donkey Kong barrel at more such GitHub repositories. body: TL;DR Google’s Android Pulse app is starting to appear as an available update in the Play Store. The background service appears to detect unusual resource usage, such as apps suddenly consuming too much battery, memory, or processing power. Android Pulse isn’t new; builds date back to March, and the Play Store shows more than 10 million downloads. There are plenty of Google apps you probably use every day, but Android Pulse is definitely not one of them. In fact, you may not even know it exists. That could change soon, though, because this mysterious system app is suddenly showing up as an available update in the Play Store. As first spotted by 9to5Google , Android Pulse is a Google-made app that works behind the scenes. Its job appears to be pretty simple: keep an eye out for apps or parts of Android that are using your phone’s resources in unusual ways.

title: I’m quitting Kindle, and Amazon’s new DRM update proves why you should too
summary: I’m finally ready to leave the Kindle world behind.
body: The Kindle Oasis was released in 2019, and it’s been a while since Amazon added a meaningful update to the system. So, when I learned that Amazon was rolling out a new system software update this past week, I was quite excited. That’s until I learned that the update closes a long-standing loophole for library books borrowed via Libby that lets you hold onto a book longer than you’d otherwise be allowed. Additionally, it further tightens DRM to ensure buyers can’t offload books from the Kindle. While the first feature doesn’t affect me much, the latter, as someone who likes preserving digital media, makes the update an instant no-go for me. On paper, these changes protect publishers’ rights and intellectual property. For the end user, though, they are just another reminder that you never truly own your digital library or even the hardware you technically bought.

title: Where are all Google’s smart displays? Out-of-stock Store listings raise eyebrows
summary: From Nest Hub to Pixel Tablet, the Google Store is out of every smart display.
body: TL;DR The online Google Store is sold out of every single smart display device. While both the Nest Hub and Hub Max simply show as unavailable, there’s an option to sign up for info on the return of Pixel Tablet sales. Google’s expect to introduce a new Google Home Display at some point in the future. In a lot of ways, today’s online Google Store experience is better than it’s ever been, including not just the latest Pixel phones and Watch , but also a ton of smart home gear. We’ve got plenty of Nest cameras , the new Google Home Speaker , and lots more. But go shopping for a new smart display, and you may spot a problem: Google doesn’t seem to have any available for sale. Product availability on the Google Store is regularly in flux, and we’re used to occasionally seeing our favorites go out of stock. Sometimes that’s just a supply chain blip, and sales resume shortly. Other times, though, like we recently saw with the Nest Mini and Nest Audio , that really does signal that Google’s done with the product for good.
